title: Stale-item self-heal: liveness-repair, not auto-resolve
summary: Agents do NOT self-heal stale graph items by default. The orchestrator is event-driven: an agent owns a task from start_task until complete_task. If it exits without reporting, that task is nobody's job — no reconciliation loop reads lastChanged/agent.state. Two distinct failure modes need DIFFERENT handling: (1) Crashed/exited agent → task stuck in_progress = genuine orphan; the only party that could report is dead, so it CANNOT self-heal. Needs a reaper: agent.state!=running AND task in_progress AND lastChanged past threshold → revert to ready for re-claim (idempotent, safe) or failed. (2) Stale tested/ready (e.g. 'Attempt A' token-cost arm) = pending verdict, NOT an orphan; the task did its job and waits on a parent/human. Auto-promoting tested→done would HIDE real failures — so SURFACE, don't auto-resolve. Design rule: reconciler does liveness repair (reap dead in_progress→ready) but only surfaces stale tested/ready. Host it as one pass at the top of each orch-loop heartbeat tick (no new always-on daemon). This is the escalation-gate roadmap item wearing a different hat — 'stale + can't self-heal → escalate' IS the gate; wire as one feature.
